items.title: 7.2 Waves ki superposition ka usool (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 7.2 with Fig. 7.4 and the noise-cancelling steps (PDF 141-143).

blocks.text: Agar medium ke kisi particle (zarre) par ek hi waqt do waves asar karein, to particle ka resultant (kul) displacement un ke alag alag displacements ka algebraic sum (plus/minus ke saath jama) hota hai. Ise principle of superposition (superposition ka usool) kehte hain.
Doosre lafzon mein, alag alag waves ke displacements aapas mein jama ho kar ek naya wave pattern banate hain, jaisa Fig. 7.4 (a aur b) mein hai.
(i) Agar ek doosre par aane wali do waves ka phase ek jaisa ho (same phase), to resultant displacement yeh hoga:
Yahan y₁ = wave 1 ka amplitude, y₂ = wave 2 ka amplitude aur y = resultant amplitude hai.
Khaas taur par agar y₁ = y₂ ho, to resultant displacement yeh hoga:

blocks.alt: Chaar qataren. Wave 1: magenta lehar, crest par chhota displacement y1. Wave 2: us ke sath qadam milati cyan lehar, displacement y2. Wave 1 and 2 superposed: dono lehrein ek axis par, crests ek sath. Resultant wave: kaali lehar, usi crest par displacement y, y = y1 + y2.
blocks.caption: Figure 7.4 (a): Ek hi frequency ki do waves ki superposition jo bilkul ek phase mein hain (kitab ki Figure 7.4 (a) ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.text: (ii) Agar ek doosre ko cross karne wali do waves ka phase ulta (opposite phase) ho, to resultant displacement yeh hoga:
Khaas taur par agar y₁ = y₂ ho, to resultant displacement y = 0 hoga.

Isi tarah agar medium ke kisi particle par ek hi waqt n waves asar karein aur har wave se us ka displacement y₁, y₂, ……, yₙ ho, to in n waves ke ek saath asar se particle ka resultant displacement y tamam displacements ka algebraic sum hai, yaani:
Isi ko waves ki superposition ka principle kehte hain. Mathematically ise yun bhi likhte hain:
Yahan y(x,t) resultant wave hai, aur y₁(x,t), y₂(x,t), ……, yₙ(x,t) alag alag waves hain.

blocks.alt: Chaar qataren. Wave 1: magenta lehar, pehle crest, displacement y1. Wave 2: utni hi cyan lehar, pehle trough, displacement y2 neeche. Wave 1 and 2 superposed: ek axis par dono lehrein ek doosre ka aaina (mirror image). Resultant wave: seedhi lakeer, y = 0.
blocks.caption: Figure 7.4 (b): Ek hi frequency ki do waves ki superposition jo bilkul ulte phase mein hain (kitab ki Figure 7.4 (b) ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: (a) mein crest crest par aata hai, is liye displacements jama hote hain: y = y₁ + y₂ (constructive). (b) mein crest trough par aata hai; jab y₁ aur y₂ barabar hon to y = y₁ − y₂ = 0 (destructive). Noise-cancelling headphones isi (b) wale usool par ‘anti-noise’ bana kar shor khatam karte hain.
Waves ki baat mein y(x,t) wave function hai, yaani kisi point x par aur waqt t par wave ka displacement. Yeh wave ki shakal aur waqt ke saath us ki tabdeeli batata hai.
Superposition ka principle linear waves ya chhote amplitude wali (small amplitude) waves par lagu hota hai.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Kitab ka yeh jumla “linear waves or small” par adhoora chhapa hai. Matlab yeh hai ke yeh usool linear waves, yaani chhote amplitude wali waves, par lagu hota hai; bohat bari (non-linear) disturbances mein displacements seedhe jama nahi hote.
Waves ki superposition se kai dilchasp phenomena (waqiaat) paida hote hain:

items: Ek jaisi frequency wali do waves jo ek hi simt (direction) mein chalein (Interference).
Thori si mukhtalif frequencies wali do waves jo ek hi simt mein chalein (Beats).
Barabar frequency wali do waves jo ulti simton mein chalein (Stationary waves).

blocks.title: Ghaur karein (Ponder Upon)
blocks.text: White light (safed roshni) se bana hua interference pattern: kitab is ki tasveer dikhati hai jis mein rang daar roshan aur andheri dhariyan (fringes) hain.
Superposition ke principle ke istemal
Waves ki superposition ka principle istemal kar ke noise-cancelling headphones na-pasandeeda shor (unwanted noise) ko khatam kar dete hain, aur sunne ka tajurba zyada pur-sukoon ho jata hai.

items: Headphones mein ek ya zyada microphones hote hain jo ird gird ka shor (ambient noise) pakarte hain, jaise peeche logon ki baatein, engine ki awaz ya mahaul ka koi bhi shor.
Microphone yeh sound signals headphones ke andar amplifier aur processing unit ko bhejta hai.
Processing unit ek "anti-noise" signal banata hai jo ird gird ke shor ka bilkul ulat hota hai (amplitude barabar, phase ulta).
Phir anti-noise signal headphones mein matlooba audio (jaise music ya awaz) ke saath chalaya jata hai.
Jab anti-noise signal ird gird ke shor se milta hai to dono waves ek doosre ko cancel (khatam) kar deti hain, aur sunne mein bohat khamoshi ho jati hai.

blocks.text: Yeh misal asal soorat-e-haal ko bohat saada kar ke batati hai, kyunke noise-cancelling headphones achhi cancellation ke liye pecheeda algorithms aur kai microphones istemal karte hain. Phir bhi un ka kaam samajhne ke liye superposition ka bunyadi principle hi asal cheez hai.

blocks.prompt: Superposition ka usool bayan kijiye aur us se noise-cancelling headphones ki wazahat kijiye (comprehensive question 7.1; MCQ 7.2). Jab do barabar waves bilkul ulat phase mein milein to nateeja kya hai?
blocks.explanation: Jab do ya zyada waves ek hi waqt kisi zarre par asar karein to us ka displacement alag displacements ka algebraic majmooa hai, y = y1 + y2 + ... + yn. Headphones ird gird ka shor record karte hain, usi amplitude magar ulat phase ka anti-noise signal banate hain aur music ke saath chalate hain; jahan dono milte hain y = y1 - y2 = 0, to shor khatam ho jata hai aur music baqi rehta hai. Bilkul ulat phase mein do barabar waves ka nateeja displacement sifar hai.

blocks.text: Mukhtasar khulasa

items: Superposition: resultant displacement = alag displacements ka algebraic sum.
Same phase: y = y₁ + y₂ (barabar hon to y = 2y₁); opposite phase: y = y₁ − y₂ (barabar hon to y = 0).
n waves: y = y₁ + y₂ + … + yₙ, ya y(x,t) = y₁(x,t) + … + yₙ(x,t).
Is se interference, beats aur stationary waves bante hain; noise-cancelling headphones anti-noise se shor cancel karte hain.
